column5: Countryside Code (England and Wales), Rights and permissions: the code lists camping, with freshwater swimming and fishing, among activities for which you may need the landowner's permission. Firms up the course's England and Wales row: outside places with specific provision (such as Dartmoor's mapped areas), ask the landowner first.

Countryside Code fires: do not light fires and only have barbecues where signs say you can; put barbecues out and make sure the ashes are cold; some land managers burn heath and moor on purpose between 1 October and 15 April; call 999 if you see an unattended fire.

Countryside Code litter and nature: take litter and food waste home, dropping litter is a criminal offence; leave rocks, plants and trees as you find them and do not disturb ground-nesting birds or historic sites. Matches the course.

Countryside Code dogs: on open access land and at the coast a dog must be on a lead around livestock, and on open access land from 1 March to 31 July even with no livestock; a farmer may shoot a dog chasing livestock; let the dog off the lead if threatened by cattle or horses. Matches the module 6 callout.

Countryside Code planning: tell someone where you are going and when you expect back, because in rural areas you may not see anyone for hours and phone signal is unreliable in many places; you are responsible for yourself and others in your care; check tides, including tidal rivers, and the Environment Agency water-quality site before swimming; do not be afraid to turn back.

Countryside Code waymarks: yellow arrow footpath (walkers and mobility aid users), blue arrow bridleway (adds horse riders and cyclists), purple arrow restricted byway (adds horse-drawn vehicles), red arrow byway open to all traffic, acorn for the 16 National Trails, round brown walker-over-hills symbol for open access land where you may leave the path; permissive paths are set by the landowner's local signs. Useful for the map-reading module, which works with the OS legend.

Countryside Code: give livestock, horses and wild animals plenty of space, especially with young; do not feed them; follow the farmer's directions when animals are moved; when walking on a road without a pavement, face oncoming traffic; take care at level crossings.
